title: Aloo Paratha (Spiced Potato-Stuffed Flatbreads) with Yoghurt
summary: A soft wholemeal dough wrapped around potato mashed with ginger, chilli, coriander and warm spices, rolled thin and griddle-cooked with ghee, served with yoghurt.
equipment: 25-28 cm cast-iron frying pan or flat griddle
baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: add the last 20 ml only if needed

ingredients.item: floury potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the two flours and 1/2 tsp salt in the bowl, then rub in the oil with your fingertips until crumbly. Add 150 ml warm water and mix to a soft dough, adding the rest only if it feels dry. Knead for 5 min until smooth, cover and rest for 30 min. Resting relaxes the gluten so the dough rolls out without springing back.

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with cold water, bring to the boil and simmer for 12-16 min until very tender. Drain well and leave to steam-dry for 2 min, then mash until completely smooth. Any lumps can tear the thin dough, and dry potato keeps the parathas from going soggy. Cool for 20 min.

steps.title: Season the filling
steps.text: Stir in the shallot, coriander, ginger, chilli, cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, lemon juice and 1 tsp salt. Divide and roll into 8 balls.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll one into a 10 cm round, set a filling ball in the middle, gather the edges up over the top and pinch firmly to seal. Turn it seam side down, flatten with your palm and roll gently on a floured surface to a 3 mm round about 18-20 cm across. Stack on the lined tray with paper between and repeat.

steps.title: Cook on the griddle
steps.text: Heat the pan over medium heat for 5 min. Cook a paratha for about 1 min until bubbles appear and it moves freely, flip and cook 1 min. Brush the top with ghee, flip and cook for about 1 min, pressing the edges with a spatula, until brown-spotted. Brush and flip again for 30-60 seconds until crisp and golden on both sides.

steps.title: Keep warm and serve
steps.text: Wrap each paratha in the tea towel while you cook the rest. Serve hot with the yoghurt.

tips: The commonest mistake is a wet filling, which bursts through the dough; drain the potatoes very well.
Roll gently from the centre outwards; pressing hard pushes the filling through.
If a little filling breaks through, patch it with a pinch of flour and carry on.
Serve with pickle, a pat of butter or a mint yoghurt.
storage: Cool, stack with baking paper and refrigerate up to 2 days, or freeze up to 2 months. Reheat in a dry pan over medium heat, 1-2 min each side, until hot through (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
